architecture.mechanism: Precise temperature control of biological samples during transportation using an insulated shipping container with stable thermal regulation to maintain a narrow, uniform temperature window for the entire shipment duration.
architecture.intervention: Adapt the insulated, high-thermal-mass passive container design (replacing battery-powered active control with pre-conditioned phase-change material tuned to a 2–8 °C setpoint and a high-thermal-capacity internal sample block) to buffer the 96-well microplate against ambient heat loads during 72-hour hot-climate land shipment.
architecture.expected_effect: Reagent temperature remains within the 2–8 °C specification across the full 72-hour transit despite external ambient temperatures typical of hot-climate land routes, eliminating thermal-excursion-driven reagent degradation while keeping the parcel lightweight and electronics-free.
architecture.falsification_test: Ship three representative parcels through a simulated ISTA 7D summer hot-climate profile (e.g., 35–45 °C ambient, 72-hour duration) with microplate wells loaded with temperature-logging probes and representative diagnostic reagent; the run passes only if all probe readings across the plate stay within 2–8 °C for the full 72 h, with inter-well uniformity ≤ 0.1 °C; if any well exceeds 8 °C or drops below 2 °C, or if the parcel mass exceeds the economic shipping threshold, the intervention fails.
